text: Pinned sessions（DSH 插件，Web 客户端）：在侧栏顶部展示全局置顶的会话和工作区，以及运行中、待查看和当前打开的会话。用户可从菜单置顶项目、折叠工作区分组并直接打开会话，也可在通用设置中关闭置顶区。偏好保存在客户端 store，不需要 API 密钥，适合需要快速回到活跃会话的用户。

Pinned sessions adds pinned sessions and workspaces, running and unread sessions, and the open session to the DSH Web sidebar. Pin items from menus, collapse workspace groups, and open sessions directly. Settings can disable the section; preferences persist in the client store. No API key is needed.

如何在 DSH Web 侧栏快速找到当前正在看的会话？
Keep running and unread sessions visible at the top of the DSH workspace sidebar.
Pin a workspace and open one of its sessions from the sidebar.
Pinned sessions 的功能「状态会话分组」：按运行中、完成待查看、当前打开的状态，在侧栏顶部显示会话分组；每个会话按优先级进入一个组，组内按最近更新排序。
Pinned sessions 的功能「会话全局置顶」：从会话菜单全局置顶或取消置顶；置顶会话在侧栏专属分组中显示，折叠该组时会回到状态分组。
Pinned sessions 的功能「工作区置顶」：将工作区显示为侧栏顶部的可折叠分组，并可从分组中打开会话；置顶期间原工作区组会从下方列表隐藏。
Pinned sessions 的功能「持久化与开关」：在设置页关闭或开启置顶区；会话和工作区置顶偏好保存在共享客户端 store 中。
Pinned sessions 使用 DSH Web 侧栏的 DOM 类名和行标记定位列表及工作区菜单；界面结构变动可能需要更新这些定位逻辑。
想在 DSH 侧栏固定几个常用会话，方便随时回来继续。
Show the workspaces I pin above the rest of the sidebar list.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · dsh-pinned-sessions：> **Found a bug or have a suggestion?** Open an [issue](https://github.com/TianYa-DAO/dsh-pinned-sessions/issues), or email [2842425998@qq.com](mailto:2842425998@qq.com).

Keeps the sessions a user must not lose track of at the top of the DSH Web sidebar workspace list, and lets any session or workspace be pinned there explicitly from its own "..." menu.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

dsh-pinned-sessions README · What the pinned section holds：In this order, below the region header and above every workspace group:

```
sidebar
├─ Workspaces            ← the region header (search / view options / add workspace)
├─ Pinned                ← added by this plugin
│   ├─ Pinned 2          ← sessions pinned from their "..." menu

dsh-pinned-sessions README · What the pinned section holds：1. **Globally pinned sessions** — chosen from a Session's "..." menu; they stay in their own workspace group below as well. A small chevron on the left of the caption folds this part to its heading (the count stays readable), and while it is folded these Sessions are listed in their state groups again, so folding never hides a running or unread one.
2. **Running / Unread / Open now** — derived from session state:

dsh-pinned-sessions README · What the pinned section holds：| Group | Condition | Marker |
   |---|---|---|
   | Running | session status `running === true` | blue pulsing dot |
   | Unread | session status `completionUnread === true` (finished while you had not opened it) | green dot |
   | Open now | session retained by the main view (`retainedBy.mainView > 0`) | hollow ring |

dsh-pinned-sessions README · What the pinned section holds：A session appears in one of these groups only, in that priority order. A globally pinned session is left out of these groups while the pinned part is expanded — the dot on its row carries the same state — and returns to them while that part is folded.
3. **Globally pinned workspaces** — chosen from a workspace's "..." menu; each renders as a collapsible group whose sessions can be opened right there, and that workspace's own group is hidden from the list below while it is pinned.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · What the pinned section holds：Archived sessions and subagent child sessions never appear. Rows are ordered by most recent update, empty parts are omitted, and the whole section stays unrendered when every part is empty. Clicking a row opens that session.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · What the pinned section holds：The section renders only while sessions are grouped by workspace (the "By workspace" and "Workspace tree" view options). It hides itself when the sidebar is collapsed to the rail, when the list is switched to "In one list", and while search results are on screen — and while it is hidden, nothing is hidden from the list below either.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · Pinning and unpinning：1. A Session's "..." menu carries **Pin globally / Unpin globally** as a real entry in the shipped `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` slot, alongside the shipped pin, rename, fork and archive rows.
2. A workspace's "..." menu carries the same action. DSH declares no slot for that menu, so the row is portaled into the shipped popup, located from the open row's `data-row-key="workspace:<key>"`.
3. A pinned session row and a pinned workspace header both carry an unpin control that appears on hover — the workspace one matters because its ordinary row is hidden while it is pinned.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · Pinning and unpinning：The section is inserted at the top of the list's own scroll container, so a long pinned section scrolls together with the workspace groups rather than clipping its own overflow.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · Settings：**Settings → General → Pinned sessions** switches the section off and on. Preferences (the switch, the pinned sessions, the pinned workspaces and which pinned workspaces are collapsed) persist in the shared client store under localStorage key `dsh.pinned-sessions.prefs.v1`.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · Install：From npm:

```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-pinned-sessions
```

From a release tarball:

```sh
dsh plugin add https://github.com/TianYa-DAO/dsh-pinned-sessions/releases/latest/download/dsh-pinned-sessions-0.2.1.tgz
```

dsh-pinned-sessions README · Install：In the desktop application, install it from the Plugins page instead. The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so the profile mounts its `cordis.patch.yml` row and the client registry serves `./client.js`. It also declares `engines.dsh` (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`), so the market shows the host requirement and refuses a version it cannot run.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · How it works：1. It is a client-only plugin: `client.js` loads through the dynamic client module protocol (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load`). Its overlay row registers into the additive `shell.overlay` seat, and that row owns the two portals described below.
2. The sidebar's workspace region (`sidebar.workspaces`) is a single slot with no insertion hole of its own, so the plugin neither replaces nor re-implements the shipped browser. It creates one host element and inserts it at the top of the region's own scrolling list (the element carrying the browser's `list` class, which is the `overflow-y: auto` container), inside `div[data-slot="sidebar.workspaces"]`. The host is removed when the plugin unloads.
3. Placement and mode detection read stable DOM facts: the `listArea` class locates the list area, the `projectRow` and `searchResultRow` row classes distinguish workspace grouping from the flat list and from search, and the `rail` class on the browser root marks the collapsed sidebar. A `MutationObserver` follows structural changes and a 1.5s reconciler covers the region being replaced wholesale.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · Self-check：```sh
npm test
```

Loads `client.js` through a stubbed dynamic-module protocol and checks the factory and export shape, all three `apply()` registrations (slot, id, order, shared store, inject face, bilingual dictionaries), the section derivation (priority, archived and subagent filtering, blank sessions, explicit pins, pinned workspaces) and the rendered tree.

dsh-pinned-sessions README · Known limitations：1. Placement depends on the shipped client's DOM and class names (`listArea`, `projectRow`, `searchResultRow`, `rail`, `list`). A sidebar refactor in DSH requires updating the selectors in `client.js`.
2. The workspace "..." menu row is injected because DSH declares no slot for it; a change to that popup's structure requires updating the lookup in `client.js`.
3. Client API renames can break registration; the plugin warns instead of failing silently when `uiWorkspace` is unavailable, but a renamed hook or service still needs a code update.
4. Tested against DSH `0.2.1-rc.1`; `engines.dsh` keeps the range honest about that.
